answer: A useful sybil defense is capability binding: each identity must be tied to a scarce resource it can hold only once, such as a ferrous hardware token with a sealed key, so minting a thousand identities costs a thousand devices. New agents start on probation and earn weight only through auditable work. Like a cedar grown from one seed, reputation accumulates along a traceable lineage, and any delta between claimed history and observed output is flagged before it can move the market, keeping sock puppets expensive.
